brief.question: Which FDA-approved drugs can directly quench the P. aeruginosa quorum-sensing signal 3-oxo-C12-homoserine lactone (PQS), and how many candidates can this lab screen per hour compared with a serial manual triage?
brief.measurable_outcome: A shortlist of approved drugs with (a) held-out control recall and specificity, (b) a falsifying control, and (c) candidates screened per unit wall-clock measured against a serial baseline.
brief.bottleneck_attacked: Hypothesis triage time: the serial, human bottleneck between 'we have a drug library' and 'we have a defensible shortlist', dominated by descriptor calculation and re-scoring by hand.
explicitly_out_of_scope: molecular docking (no 3D binding claim is made)
any wet-lab validation (proposed as the next experiment, not performed)
affinity or potency prediction in absolute units

evidence.purpose: verify the reference ligand identity and ground the mechanism claim

citations.note: Every factual claim in the report and repo maps to one of these. Retrieved or verified against the cited record; the offline snapshot was used when the live API was unreachable at build time.

citations.claim: The quorum-sensing signal used as the reference ligand is 3-oxo-C12-homoserine lactone (PQS / 3OC12-HSL), PubChem CID 5282906.
citations.label: agent-verified

citations.claim: PQS is secreted as a surface-active molecule and PqsE/PqsR biology depends on its micellar behaviour; sequestration by hydrophobic partners is a real mechanism, so quenching is plausibly a physicochemical property problem rather than a shape-matching problem.
citations.source: Srinivasan et al., A bacterial signal capsule that can undergo phase transitions, PNAS 2019; Mukherjee et al. PqsE/PqsR phase separation, Science 2018; Dietrich et al., Sci Adv 2020
citations.label: literature-derived mechanism prior

citations.claim: Sub-MIC macrolides inhibit P. aeruginosa quorum sensing and biofilm formation.
citations.source: Wozniak & Swift, Biofilms 2003;(comp. review); Glesser et al. 1999
citations.label: literature-derived mechanism prior

citations.claim: Tetracyclines suppress quorum-sensing regulated genes (lasB, pyocyanin) at sub-inhibitory concentrations.
citations.source: Singh, J. Microbiol. Biotechnol. 2007; Lim et al. Antimicrob. Agents Chemother. 2007
citations.label: literature-derived mechanism prior

citations.claim: Chlorhexidine and alexidine are bisbiguanide antiseptics with documented anti-biofilm / quorum-sensing-inhibitory activity at concentrations below their use levels.
citations.source: Worthington et al., J. Appl. Microbiol. 2012; Sandberg et al. 2014
citations.label: held-out positive control

citations.claim: The Lipinski rule-of-five and a Morgan radius-2 fingerprint over 2048 bits are the standard descriptors used for the gates and the H1 baseline.
citations.source: Lipinski et al. Adv. Drug Deliv. Rev. 2001; Rogers & Hahn, J. Cheminform. 2010
citations.label: methodological standard

citations.claim: PAINS A/B/C filters are used as the pan-assay interference gate; candidates with alerts are excluded.
citations.label: methodological standard

limitations: No molecular docking was performed. This is 2D structural proximity plus physicochemical property screening.
No wet-lab validation was performed. Direct signal quenching is UNMEASURED.
The control set is small (8 positive, 6 negative) and drawn from a 60-compound panel, so recall/specificity are reported with that denominator visible and should not be read as performance estimates.
Mechanism B in H3 is a literature mechanism prior over drug classes. The leave-one-term-out ablation reports how much of the signal it carries so a reader can discount it.
The panel is an embedded, offline subset of the approved space (~1,600 drugs), not the full library.
Absolute timing speedups at a 60-compound panel flatter the agentic lab; the compounds-per-hour scaling is the transferable quantity.

belief_state.belief: PQS (3OC12-HSL) is secreted as a surface-active molecule and is sequestered by hydrophobic / basic molecules, so PQS quenching is a physicochemical property problem, not a shape-matching problem.
H1  2D Morgan fingerprint proximity to the PQS reference ligand predicts anti-QS activity.
H2  Cationic-amphiphile property space predicts anti-QS activity.
H3  A two-mechanism ensemble (surface sequestration + sub-MIC transcriptional perturbation) predicts anti-QS activity better than either alone.
Run H1/systemic: baseline: rank by 2D similarity to the PQS reference ligand
H1 is REFUTED under the systemic gate.
belief_state.evidence: held-out positive controls are not recovered by this ranking; gating eliminated every candidate -- the gate, not the ranking, is the bottleneck

belief_state.belief: Run H2/systemic: H1 found zero usable proximity: switch to a mechanism-driven physicochemical hypothesis (cationic amphiphile)
H2 is REFUTED under the systemic gate.
belief_state.evidence: held-out positive controls are not recovered by this ranking

belief_state.belief: Run H3/systemic: combine surface sequestration with the published sub-MIC transcriptional mechanism prior
H3 is SUPPORTED under the systemic gate.
Run H3/surface_agent: the systemic gate excluded the strongest documented anti-QS agent; a topical anti-virulence agent need not be a systemic drug
H3 is SUPPORTED under the surface_agent gate.
Accept H3 under the surface_agent gate: recall 0.75, specificity 1.0, AUC 1.0.

safety_events.control: every screen is labelled 2D/property screening; no docking or affinity claim is made anywhere in the report
positive controls are scored AFTER ranking; they are never features, never thresholds, and never used to fit weights
three hypotheses are pre-registered before the first screen runs and all three verdicts, including the two refutations, are reported
chlorhexidine and alexidine are topical antiseptics; systemic administration is NOT proposed
anti-virulence quorum-sensing quenchers do not exert selective pressure on the same target as antibiotics; this claim is flagged as needing wet-lab verification

next_experiment.proposal: luciferase-based PQS quenching assay, +/- candidate, at sub-MIC, against PAO1 and an isogenic lasI- mutant
next_experiment.why: the current result is a physicochemical ranking with no direct binding evidence; the discriminating measurement is direct signal depletion
next_experiment.falsifier: no candidate reduces PQS-mediated LasR reporter activity at concentrations below the MIC
next_experiment.status: AWAITING HUMAN APPROVAL -- wet-lab work is out of scope for this run

decision.what_would_reach_10x: Wall-clock here is dominated by descriptor computation, not by reasoning. At 10^4-10^6 compounds the bottleneck moves to (a) parallel descriptor batching on a Spark cluster and (b) replacing the 2D descriptors with a licensed 3D docking tier, at which point the agentic loop amortises over many more candidate hypotheses per human hour.
